caveat: Maltodextrin has a Glycemic Index (GI ~110–185) significantly higher than table sugar (GI ~65). Products marketed as 'No Added Sugar' containing maltodextrin can trigger rapid blood glucose spikes in diabetic consumers.
source: American Diabetes Association; Harvard Health Publishing Glycemic Index Guidelines

common_substitute: High Fructose Corn Syrup (HFCS) / Liquid Glucose
caveat: Liquid glucose/HFCS is rapidly processed by the liver, promoting hepatic lipogenesis and elevated triglyceride levels compared to natural whole-food sugars.
source: NIH National Library of Medicine - Fructose Metabolism and Hepatic Steatosis

caveat: While zero-calorie, recent clinical studies indicate high habitual intake may alter gut microbiome composition and modulate insulin sensitivity.
source: Nature Microbiology & WHO Guideline on Non-Sugar Sweeteners (NSS)

caveat: Strictly contraindicated for individuals with Phenylketonuria (PKU) due to inability to metabolize phenylalanine. Classified as 2B 'possibly carcinogenic' by IARC.
Sugar alcohols may cause severe osmotic bloating, gas, and laxative effects in sensitive individuals when consumed in quantities exceeding 10–20g/day.
source: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) Polyol Evaluation

caveat: Palm fractions contain up to 50% palmitic acid (saturated fat) and industrial processing may introduce trace MCPD esters; increases LDL cholesterol.
source: WHO Guidelines on Saturated Fatty Acid Intake; EFSA Contaminants in Food Chain

caveat: Presents severe hyperkalemia risks for individuals with chronic kidney disease (CKD) or those taking ACE inhibitors and potassium-sparing diuretics.
source: American Heart Association Potassium Salt Advisory

caveat: Gluten-free substitutes often rely on pure refined starches with near-zero dietary fiber, resulting in rapid postprandial glycemic excursions.
